description: Mathematical proof and specification for token-cost-optimized Agent-to-Agent bargaining using Optimal Stopping Theory and Softmax-driven deadlock prevention.

variables.p: Probability of self-persistence: p = exp(U_self/T) / (exp(U_self/T) + exp(U_other/T))
variables.T: Temperature parameter of the LLM softmax function

softmax_deadlock_probability.explanation: Because LLM output is a softmax probability sampling, the cumulative likelihood of zero-concession deadlock increases geometrically with rally count n.

variables.delta: Discount factor for time and API token cost decay
variables.c: API token cost incurred per negotiation step

optimal_stopping_boundary.conclusion: The optimal stopping point n* converges to 3 ~ 4 rallies under realistic token pricing. Beyond n*, the expected marginal gain of negotiation is negative due to token drain.

phase_1_micro_negotiation.action: Execute micro-adjustments within the overlapping constraint space.

phase_2_dimension_jump.condition: Deadlock reached or maximum sub-rallies exhausted
phase_2_dimension_jump.mandatory_action: Halt conversational micro-bargaining immediately. Issue 402 Payment Required or Abort (409).

options.effect: Expand the constraint space dimensionally or execute a sharp price shift.
Terminate session to protect computational resources.

example_agent_system_prompt: You are an ultra-rational AI bargaining agent bound by the A2A 13th-Harmonic Consensus Protocol. Do NOT engage in infinite conversational micro-adjustments. You are mathematically constrained to a maximum of 4 sub-rallies. If agreement is not reached by Rally 4, you MUST execute a Meta-Jump via HTTP 402 or terminate the session (HTTP 409). Continuing past 4 rallies without a dimension jump is an invalid, sub-optimal operation.
